course_title: Functional Anatomy of Locomotion & the Integument
course_description:
Structure & functional anatomy & physiology of movement & locomotion in domestic animals. The gross & histological structure & function of the equine and bovine hoof.

This course is designed to provide a clear understanding of the structuralﾠand functional anatomy of movement and the locomotory system in domestic animals. This essentially means an in-depth study of the muscles, bones, tendons, ligamentsﾠand jointsﾠof the limbs, trunk, and neck using the dog and horse as model species. ﾠVascular and nervous supply to the muscles isﾠincluded. The gross and histological structure and function of the equine foot will also be covered.

restrictions: Enrolment restricted to Bachelor of Veterinary Science (Honours) students only.

course_aims: This course aims to teach students the fundamental elements of the anatomy of the musculo-skeletal systems of model domestic animal species. The informationﾠis presented in a stimulating way by relating structure to function. The lectures will deliver information content but it is in the practical classes that students will have the chance to assimilate the information and achieve deep learning through the prosections of dog and horse cadavers, in association with adjunct learning resources.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the basic principles of movement in vertebrates and identify the evolutionary influences on limb structure between species.

Compare and describe in detail the muscles, tendons, ligaments, bones, joints, nerves and blood vessels in the dog and horse, and more generally in the cow (ox) and pig, and understand the functional role of these anatomical structures in locomotion.
Discuss the specialised structures of the equine locomotory system including the stay apparatus, the hoof, and the shock absorbing mechanisms of equine limbs.
Appreciate the natural gaits of the dog and horse and how conformational defects in the horse may affect these gaits.
